A Typst document now opens as the pages it compiles to. More at
[www.malgel.com](https://www.malgel.com).

## New

- **Typst.** A `.typ` file opens as the document it compiles to. The Typst
  compiler that already exports Malgel's PDFs runs on the source in-process,
  so nothing extra needs installing, and the pages are shown in the same
  viewer a PDF uses: continuous scrolling, fit-width / fit-page / custom
  zoom, one page or two side by side, page thumbnails, and a drag to move
  around once zoomed in.
  - Files the document names resolve next to it, so a document spread over
    several files compiles as one — and only what it names is reachable.
  - The preview is recompiled when the source changes on disk, so it follows
    an editor that is not this one: a `typst watch` workflow, a terminal
    editor, another window on the same file.
  - A source that no longer compiles keeps the last version on screen and
    says so, instead of going blank.

## Downloads

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS 11+ (Apple silicon) | `Malgel-0.1.10-macos-arm64.dmg`: open it and drag Malgel to Applications |
| Windows 10+ | `Malgel-0.1.10-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `Malgel-0.1.10-windows-x64.zip` (portable) |
| Linux x86_64 | `Malgel-0.1.10-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or `malgel-0.1.10-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

The macOS app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so Gatekeeper blocks it after download: right-click it and choose Open once, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Malgel.app`. The Windows files are unsigned: SmartScreen may warn, and **More info → Run anyway** gets past it. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every file's checksum.
